question: Life expectancy in India was 58.6 years in 1990, which increased to ________ in 2023, the highest recorded since the inception of this index.
solution:
The correct answer is __**72 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Life expectancy** refers to the average number of years a person is expected to live based on statistical data. This metric is widely used to gauge the health and quality of life in a country.
 
• In **1990**, India's life expectancy was recorded at **58.6 years**, reflecting challenges in healthcare, sanitation, and nutrition during that time. *This statement is correct.*
 
• By **2023**, India achieved its **highest recorded life expectancy** of **72 years**, showcasing significant improvements in healthcare infrastructure, public health initiatives, and economic growth. *This statement is correct.*
 
• The increase in life expectancy is attributed to factors such as advancements in medical science, better access to healthcare services, improved nutrition, and reduced infant mortality rates.
 
• Option **72 years** is the correct answer because it aligns with the latest data on India's life expectancy as of **2023**. The other options (70 years, 65 years, and 75 years) do not match the officially recorded figure.
 
• **Life expectancy** is an essential indicator used by organizations such as the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** and the **World Health Organization (WHO)** for assessing human development and public health globally.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 72 years.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Life Expectancy Trends:**

 
 
• India's life expectancy has steadily risen over the decades due to investments in healthcare systems, immunization programs, and public health campaigns.
 
• In **1950**, life expectancy was approximately **41 years**, highlighting the challenges faced post-Independence. By **1990**, it had risen to **58.6 years**, and by **2023**, reached **72 years**.
 
• The increase reflects improvements in sanitation, nutrition, maternal healthcare, and disease prevention efforts.
 
 
 
• **Global Comparison:**
 
 
• India's life expectancy of **72 years** in **2023** is close to the global average of **73 years**, as reported by the **United Nations**.
 
• Countries such as **Japan** and **Switzerland** have some of the highest life expectancies globally, exceeding **83 years**, due to advanced healthcare systems and higher living standards.
 
 
 
• **Factors Contributing to Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• Key contributors include access to healthcare, economic development, education, and public health programs such as vaccination drives and disease prevention campaigns.
 
• The reduction in **infant mortality rates**, improved maternal care, and better management of chronic diseases have positively impacted life expectancy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UNDP and WHO Reports:**

 
 
• Life expectancy is a key indicator in the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, which evaluates countries based on health, education, and income metrics.
 
• **WHO reports** emphasize the role of universal healthcare coverage in improving life expectancy.
 
 
 
• **India’s Healthcare Initiatives:**
 
 
• Programs such as **Ayushman Bharat** and **National Health Mission** have contributed to better healthcare access and improved life expectancy.
 
• The government's focus on **non-communicable diseases (NCDs)** and preventive healthcare has played a significant role.
